1 kamaHa Ald~aAb~apa * , [aor.
kamaHa ,] (inf. n. kamoHN; M) and ↓ A^akomaHahaA; i. q. kabaHahaA (A 'Obeyd, K) and A^akobaHahaA: (A 'Obeyd:) or kamaHa Ald~aAb~apa biAlil~jaAmi signifies He pulled in the horse, or the like, by the bridle and bit, in order that it might stop, and not run: (M:) and ↓ AkmHhA, he pulled its bridle so that its head became upright, or erect. (As, S, M.)

4 A^akomaHa See 1. -A2- AkmH Alkaromu The grape-vine became in a state of commotion preparatory to its putting forth its leaves. (S, K.) ― -b2- AkmHt Alz~amaEapu The gem, or knot, in the place whence a bunch of grapes was about to grow forth became white, and what resembled cotton came forth upon it. (Az, on the authority of Et-Táïfee.) ― -b3- See also Akmx and A^uqomiHa.

kawomaHN * (and kuwmaHN, L) A man (S) having large buttocks. (S, L, K.) ― -b2- Also kawomaHN, A man (TA) whose teeth fill his mouth so that his speech is thick: (K:) or a man whose teeth are crowded together, one upon another, so that his mouth seems to be straitened by them. (IDrd.) ― -b3- famN kwmH A mouth straitened by the great number of the teeth and by the swelling of the gums. (IDrd.)
